The equation is:
\[ u_t + \left(\frac{u^2}{2}\right)_x = {\bf N}[u] \]
This is the inviscid Burgers' equation ($u_t + uu_x = 0$) with a source term ${\bf N}[u]$.
Wave breaking (or shock formation) occurs when the spatial derivative $u_x$ becomes unbounded in finite time. Specifically, for classical solutions to the inviscid Burgers' equation, the characteristic curves intersect, leading to the formation of discontinuities. In the context of generalized solutions, this is often characterized by the gradient blowing up.

For a classical solution $u(t, x)$, wave breaking is defined as the time $T^*$ at which $\inf_{x \in \mathbb{R}} u_x(t, x) \to -\infty$ as $t \to T^{*-}$. This corresponds to the steepening of the wave front until the slope becomes infinitely negative.
